questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was far away, so I could try to live in another culture. Therefore I choose North America, where Vancouver did not disappoint. It is an amazing city, and the University is equally amazing. That was another aspect of my motivation, to try a semester at a top-50 University in the world, and UBC did not disappoint in this manner.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The UBC team for international students are very helpful, which made it way easier. They provided me with the useful information, and whenever I had any questions, I just asked them for help, and they helped me every time. UBC is an awesome choice, if you are afraid you will not know all the needed stuff before arrival, because their team can help you out easily.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got invited to an information meeting for international students, where I meet the team physically, and they provided me and other students with all the information needed. They also gave me physical documents with information on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: UBC offers a lot of housing, and all the international students I met was offered housing on campus (Term 2). I lived in Walter Gage Towers, which was totally fine for me during my stay.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Most international students live on campus, so it is my strongest recommendation to do so as well. But remember to bring everything for the rooms, including duvet, pillow and so on. You will love together with both domestic and international students, which is very nice!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before I got there I had to wish for 10 courses, where I got 6 of them. I only needed 4, so I had to drop 2. During the first two weeks of classes you can swap between courses with empty spaces, so it is a good idea to try different classes during these weeks, so you end up with courses you enjoy the most.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office was very helpful, and the professors are as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted, but there were many classes with empty spaces I could have taken that seemed interesting, so overall it was easy to be succesful here,

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try something different during the first two weeks, where you can change courses. Talk with the professors and TA's about what to expect. They are there to help you!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is quite similar to the level of the courses on UCPH. They do focus on different aspects though. In Political Science, UCPH focuses a lot on methodology and theories. where UBC focuses more on a specific empirical phenomenon.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very different. It is only professors who teach, and most courses have attendance as a part of your grade. The grade is determined by many different aspects, including midterms, attendance and the final exam, among many things. Most of the exams and midterms are written in hand.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLI321 - Chinese Politics and Development
POLI369B - Politics of Outer Space
POLI370A - Negotiations
POLI370D - Civil Wars

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all my courses, but I would really suggest POLI369B - Politics of Outer Space and POLI370A - Negotiations, as they are very different from what you can get at UCPH. I looked forward to all most every lecture in these courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had planned in detail, so did not get any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out was less expensive, but in general Vancouver is very, very expensive, so use some time to apply for grants!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many - I played in the Intramurals, where I played soccer, I joined the film society. and the gym facilities was very good!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a free-agent team for the intramurals, in whatever sport you like the most!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: So many things to do! Most people ski, hike or enjoy the beautiful nature, or watch sports such as the Whitecaps or the Cannucks

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - put on an open mind and you will be good.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live on campus! And don't be afraid to talk to people after classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People from North America is sometimes a bit superficial, so you need to make an effort.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way that they care about many different sports

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Live on campus, be open to meet canadian people, join a team for intramurals

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No :D

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To learn new things about myself, study in a different environment, and experience the amazing canadian nature!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To meet new people - but it went well anyway!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
